chose: A spoken cards essay is the same cut list (some-ui.cut-list/2) with one optional field on a shot, `spoken`: the intro (`said`), a scene (`chapter` and `narration`) or the close (`said`). The cheat-sheet series' version 2, which adds the captions design, is what makes an essay spoken: in it every scene must say something, the first is the intro and only the last may be the close. Version 1 stays silent and refuses `spoken`. The intro and close are scenes with a card picture of their own, so they show something while they are said. `durationMs` is still written but the take sets each scene's length. Each scene's chapter line is said as its own take over the scene's card, as a scene of its own (`<id>-chapter`), and its narration follows in a second take, cut in over the same card. Each chapter line marks a chapter in the upload's description, and the close is marked "What to do next".
options: an optional `spoken` field on a shot, gated by cheat-sheet v2, the chapter line its own take
a new cut-list schema, some-ui.cut-list/3, with a separate list of lines
top-level intro and close fields, and chapter and narration said as one take per scene
gray: The owner set what is said (C370); the coordinator asked for the smallest schema change and left its shape to the session. Whether the intro and close are scenes, whether durationMs stays written, and whether a chapter line is heard as its own beat are the owner's to notice when writing or watching an essay.
undo: Have cardsLines join chapter and narration into one line per scene; to drop the shape, pin cheat-sheet v3 without the captions design and drop the `spoken` checks from parseCardsEssay. The field is optional, so no essay breaks.
